subject: Operations
title: Ishikawa and the Fishbone
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ishikawa and the Fishbone.

hook.text: Kaoru Ishikawa drew a fish skeleton on a whiteboard. Each bone was a cause. The head was the problem.

buildup.text: The fishbone diagram organizes causes into categories: people, methods, machines, materials, and environment.

discovery.text: Teams brainstorm causes along each bone. The visual structure prevents jumping to conclusions.

twist.text: Ishikawa also pioneered quality circles—small worker groups that solve problems themselves, not top-down.

climax.text: Japanese factories adopted quality circles by the millions. Workers became partners in quality.

punchline.text: Give workers a diagram and they find the fix.

quiz.question: What does an Ishikawa diagram look like?
